intro: Picture this: you finish your shift at a factory in the Amata estate, drive or take the shuttle a few minutes, and you're back in a room with a small kitchen to heat up dinner, a balcony to hang laundry, a convenience store right at the front of the building, and a coin-operated washing machine so you never have to lug your clothes far — Room 9 Residence is a small serviced apartment in Pluak Daeng Moo 5 that sits right opposite the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone and close to the Amata City estate · what guests keep mentioning is the clean, move-in-ready rooms with a kitchen and balcony, available to rent daily or monthly, at a price you can actually afford, plus wide parking for around 80 cars and key-card security · it has around 12 rooms of about 25 square metres, from roughly THB 900–1,000/night, scored around 7.8 from 27 reviews on Agoda.

body.html: Who Room 9 Residence is really for — to put it as simply as possible, Room 9 Residence is accommodation built mainly for "people working in the industrial estates," not a seaside holiday hotel · it's a small serviced apartment of around 12 rooms, deliberately positioned opposite the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone and close to the Amata City estate in Pluak Daeng, a factory district where large numbers of both Thai and foreign staff come to work · the owner designed it for working-age employees who want a clean, move-in-ready room at a low price with an easy commute to the factory, since many estates in the area run staff shuttles · the people it suits best are those who have just moved here for a new job and haven't found a long-term rental yet, so they want to stay daily or monthly for now, engineers or subcontractors coming in for short projects in the estate, and people driving through who need a place to spend the night near the factory without heading all the way into Chonburi city or Rayong · on the flip side, if you're looking for a hotel with a swimming pool, a gym, a breakfast buffet or a resort atmosphere for a holiday, this isn't the answer, and you'd be better off considering a hotel in Chonburi city or around Bang Saen–Pattaya · honestly, Room 9 Residence sells "genuinely usable" at a price working people can pay every month, rather than selling luxury or a view.

Location and getting around — this is the main reason people choose to stay here · Room 9 Residence is at 659 Moo 5, Pluak Daeng Subdistrict, Pluak Daeng District, on the border between Chonburi and Rayong, in a zone locals lump together as "opposite the estate" · the standout point is that it's opposite the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone and close to the Amata City estate, along with nearby estates and industrial parks such as Bowin, Siam Eastern and Hemaraj (WHA), many of which run staff shuttles in and out by shift, so workers staying here have an easy commute to the factory · for longer trips: from Pluak Daeng you can take Highway 331 or the motorway into Chonburi city and Pattaya in about 40 minutes to 1 hour depending on your destination, while Rayong town itself lies further south · on airports, it's about 40 kilometres from U-Tapao Airport (UTP), roughly a 40–50 min drive, which is handy for foreigners flying in for short-term work · one thing worth knowing is that Pluak Daeng is an industrial zone, not a tourist area — the restaurants and shops around you lean toward made-to-order eateries, the market in front of the estate, and convenience stores rather than cafés or big malls, so having your own car makes life much easier.

"I stayed monthly when I'd just moved here for an estate job. The room was clean, it had a small kitchen so I could heat up my own meals, the parking was spacious, and there was a convenience store out front so I could still grab food even after finishing late — well worth what I paid each month."

Room types and decor — Room 9 Residence is a small building with around 12 rooms, mostly identical studios of about 25 square metres · what sets it apart from ordinary rentals in the estate area is that the rooms come fully furnished and ready to move into right away — a bed, a wardrobe or clothes rail, a desk, a TV, a fridge, and importantly a small kitchen corner where you can cook or heat up your own food, which is a big deal for workers wanting to save on monthly food costs · many rooms have a private balcony for hanging laundry and catching the breeze · on the equipment the owner highlights: energy-saving LG air conditioning and a 3,700-watt instant water heater that delivers water hot and strong enough for a shower after your shift, plus good-quality UV-blocking curtains · the bathroom is the easy-to-use kind, with basic toiletries provided · the decor is simple and clean, function over flashy design, which fits the working-age clientele looking for value · one thing to understand is that at 25 sqm and being a studio, the room is compact and best suited to one person or a couple — it isn't spacious like a big hotel's suite, but the layout uses the space well and doesn't feel cramped.

Amenities and common areas — since it's a serviced apartment rather than a resort hotel, Room 9 Residence has no swimming pool or gym, but it focuses on what workers actually use every day · starting with the parking, which counts as a real strength — there's a car park for around 80 cars, some of it covered, plus separate motorbike parking, which is hard to find at this rental price · there's an on-site convenience store so you can buy food and essentials even after finishing work late, a coin-operated washing machine and laundry service, a water dispenser, a small garden and terrace to sit and relax, plus a hair salon on the premises · for internet there's free high-speed Wi-Fi throughout the building · on the security side it's well covered, with a 24-hour service counter, a key-card room-entry system, CCTV and 24-hour security staff, which matters a great deal to people working late shifts or women staying alone · overall the amenities here are designed to "keep daily life running smoothly" rather than to serve as leisure facilities.

Food and nearby eateries — Room 9 Residence has no restaurant or hotel-style breakfast service, which is normal for serviced apartments in an estate area · but what helps a lot is that the rooms have a small kitchen for cooking or heating up your own food, and there's an on-site convenience store for a quick bite · for restaurants nearby, the Pluak Daeng area opposite the estate has made-to-order eateries, rice-and-curry shops, noodle stalls, and the market in front of the estate that opens on a schedule, all reasonably priced and suited to workers · many people choose to take food back to eat in their room since there's a kitchen and fridge ready to go, which saves a lot on food when staying monthly · if you want a coffee shop, a café or a big mall, you may have to drive out toward Chonburi city, Pattaya or Rayong, which takes a fair while · honestly, food isn't the selling point here, but the location near cheap estate-side eateries and the in-room kitchen mean eating isn't a problem for workers used to cooking for themselves or buying takeaway.

Service — given its size as a small apartment, the service at Room 9 Residence is more casual and personal than at a big hotel chain · there's a 24-hour service counter and staff who handle entry and exit, security and any on-the-spot issues · the overall word from guests is that the team is easy to talk to and helpful with the basics, such as bookings, payment and maintenance requests · since the place caters mainly to monthly guests, enquiries and bookings tend to go through direct channels like phone, the property's website, and the Room9 Residence Facebook page rather than only through booking platforms · the right expectation to set is that there's no hotel-level service here — no room service, concierge or bellboy — it's a self-managed, look-after-yourself kind of place, which suits workers already used to apartment living.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — Room 9 Residence is a small property with relatively few reviews on the platforms (Agoda around 7.8 from 27 reviews, with similar scores elsewhere), but the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: the rooms are clean and move-in ready, the small kitchen and fridge help save on food, the parking is spacious with motorbike spots too, the on-site convenience store is very handy for anyone finishing late, the key-card system and CCTV make it feel safe, and the location near the estate makes the commute to work easy · on the watch-out side: the recurring point is that it sits in the middle of an industrial zone, so there are no attractions or cafés around and it's fairly quiet outside working hours, the 25 sqm room is compact and better for one person or a couple than a group, there's no hotel-style pool or gym, and at times availability is limited because regular monthly guests stay long-term · these gripes are more about "whether it fits your needs" than actual flaws, because this place was meant as workers' accommodation from the start.

"I came for a two-month project in the estate and picked this place because it's near the factory and has parking. The room wasn't fancy but it was clean, the hot water was strong and the internet worked fine. The only downside is how quiet it is around here — nothing to do, so after work you just come back and sleep."

Price and value — Room 9 Residence's daily rate is around THB 900–1,000/night for a 25 sqm studio with a kitchen and balcony, which is very reasonable for what you get · where it gets genuinely worthwhile is the monthly rental option, where the per-night price drops well below the daily rate, ideal for workers who need to stay for a month or several — combined with having a kitchen to cook for yourself, the rent plus food cost per month ends up far lower than staying in a hotel by the night · compared with 4-star hotels and serviced apartments in the estate area like Kameo Hotel Amata Bangpakong, or hotels in Chonburi city that start around THB 1,200 and up with a pool and breakfast, Room 9 Residence is in a different category — it's the budget option for someone who just needs a clean, safe room close to work within a budget they can control every month, not a place for extra comforts or a holiday · if your brief is "stay near the estate as cheaply as possible while still being clean and safe," the value here is well judged for that group.

What to know before you book — a few things will make your stay go more smoothly · one, this place caters to monthly guests, so availability for daily stays can be limited at times — it's best to book ahead by phone, the website, or the property's Facebook page directly, especially if you want a long stay · two, some booking channels (OTAs) list this as adults only, so check the terms on guests and bringing children clearly before booking · three, this is accommodation in an industrial area with no attractions around — if you're coming to sightsee, pick a hotel in Chonburi city or by the coast instead · four, having your own car makes things much easier, since big shops and malls are far away, but the upside is the spacious parking here · five, ask about the key/key-card deposit and refund terms clearly, since this type of property often has different conditions from a regular hotel · six, confirm that the room you book has the balcony and kitchen you want, as some rooms may differ slightly in detail.

The verdict — taking all the real reviews together, Room 9 Residence is the best fit for workers in the Pluak Daeng–Amata industrial estates who want a clean, safe room with a kitchen, close to the factory, at a low price either daily or monthly · its strengths are the location opposite Amata City and the Eastern Seaboard, move-in-ready rooms with a kitchen and balcony, parking for around 80 cars, an on-site convenience store, and a key-card security system with 24-hour CCTV · if you're after a hotel with a swimming pool, breakfast or a resort atmosphere for a holiday, this isn't the answer, and you should choose a hotel in Chonburi city or around Bang Saen–Pattaya instead · but for the right brief — staying near your work in the estate affordably and with peace of mind on security — Room 9 Residence does its job well at a price working people can afford, which is why it has so many regulars staying long-term.

faq.q: Where is Room 9 Residence, and which estates is it near?
faq.a: The property is at 659 Moo 5, Pluak Daeng Subdistrict, Pluak Daeng District, on the Chonburi–Rayong border · it sits opposite the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone and close to the Amata City estate, along with Bowin and Hemaraj · it's about 40 kilometres from U-Tapao Airport, and you can reach Chonburi city or Pattaya in about 40–60 minutes.

faq.q: Does Room 9 Residence rent daily or monthly, and how much is it?
faq.a: You can rent both daily and monthly · daily stays start at about THB 900–1,000/night for a 25 sqm studio with a kitchen and balcony · the monthly per-night rate is far cheaper than daily, ideal for estate workers on a long stay — we'd suggest asking by phone, via the website, or through the property's Facebook directly.

faq.q: What's in the rooms at Room 9 Residence?
faq.a: The rooms are studios of around 25 sqm, fully furnished and move-in ready, with a bed, desk, TV, fridge, a small kitchen corner, a private balcony, energy-saving LG air con, and a strong 3,700-watt water heater plus UV-blocking curtains · it's built for genuine everyday use by workers rather than for luxury.

faq.q: Who is Room 9 Residence good for?
faq.a: It's the best fit for workers in the Pluak Daeng–Amata estates, engineers, and subcontractors coming in for projects who want a clean, safe room with a kitchen, near the factory, at a low price · if you're coming for a holiday and want a swimming pool or breakfast, choose a hotel in Chonburi city or by the coast instead.

faq.q: Does Room 9 Residence have parking, and is it safe?
faq.a: Yes — there's spacious parking for around 80 cars, some of it covered, plus separate motorbike parking · on security there's a key-card room-entry system, CCTV, a 24-hour service counter, and 24-hour security staff, which late-shift workers and those staying alone value.

faq.q: How can I book Room 9 Residence?
faq.a: You can book through platforms like Agoda and Booking.com (some channels list it as adults only) · but for monthly stays, we'd recommend contacting them directly by phone on 092-267-1321 / 033-060-289, via the website room9residence.com, or through the Room9 Residence Facebook page, since you get the monthly rate and can check availability more directly.
